newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to woo foreign firms with quartz find.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to woo foreign firms with quartz find.

text.p: Sri Lanka will use a recent find of high quality silica quartz in its south to attract foreign investment into the region, a senior government official said on Thursday.

"We have found deposits of a very high quality silica quartz which is considered sufficient to serve the global electronics industry for the next few decades," Navin Gooneratne, chairman and director general of the Southern Development Authority (SDA), told Reuters.
The deposits, with 99.8 percent purity, have been found in Hambantota and Monaragala districts 238 km (150) miles south of capital Colombo.

Since exporting quartz without adding value is prohibited by Sri Lankan law, the SDA is promoting foreign investment from companies making fibre optics, cameras and microscopic lenses, ceramic products, computer chips and lead crystal, Gooneratne said.

"With at least two tonnes already available and about another five tonnes in reserve and a shortfall of the raw material expected in the world in about five years, these are good industries to promote," he said.
The SDA has been set up to develop Sri Lanka's southern Ruhunu region under a $3.5 billion plan which includes infrastructure and job creation.
